characterization_methods.key_findings: κ-carbide (L′1₂) appears as elongated, roughly parallel rods/platelets; Fe is low and C high inside κ, Mn nearly flat (~22–25 at.%), Al slightly enriched (~15–18 at.%); ~8 periodic κ bands over 100 nm traverse.
Fine checkerboard/tweed contrast of dark, roughly perpendicular lamellae; individual lamellae are narrower than 20 nm.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.key_findings: TE ~10% at 8Al for the 600 °C/24 h condition.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: measurement of YS, UTS, and total elongation

defect_interactions.interaction_type: Orowan bypassing of longitudinal κ-carbide rods and dislocation loop expansion, assisted by cross-slip; minor shearing of κ-carbides
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Higher dislocation densities within dislocation bundles arise from minor topological differences in spacing between κ-carbide rods; dislocations follow preferential soft paths in widest channels; stress can be high enough to shear κ-carbide interfaces.

interfaces.phase_evolution: κ-carbides are thermally very stable at 600 °C and prevail after 100 h heat treatment with only modest coarsening

phase_interfaces.coherence: lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix; forms cuboidal nanoprecipitates (near-coherent)

interfaces.slip_behavior: planar slip localization linked to κ-carbides

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: YS, UTS, and hardness after 24 h aging compared with the as-homogenized state of Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al
comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: twice as high as in the as-homogenized state (~2×)

processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting (VIM) furnace, casting into Cu molds
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five different alloys synthesized in one operation; melt from a 4-kg ingot; Al charged through an air lock after each cast.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 10×50×130 mm³ blocks to 2±0.1 mm thick, ~500 mm long sheets

processing_steps.method: cutting perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: tensile specimens prepared from segments by package spark erosion

precipitates.coherency: lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix
precipitates.distribution: regularly arranged, periodically spaced (~8 κ bands over 100 nm traverse)

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized austenitic (γ) matrix containing nm-sized κ-carbide (L′1₂) precipitates formed during aging; κ-carbides appear as elongated, roughly parallel rods/platelets.

unmapped_findings: Aging of Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al for 24 h further increases YS, UTS, and hardness to levels twice as high as in the as-homogenized state and drastically reduces ductility (b0024).

For Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al, aging for 1 h leads to an increase in YS, UTS, and hardness (increasing with temperature) and only a minor reduction in TE; the 24 h aging produces the strongest strengthening but drastically reduced ductility (b0024).
The observed strengthening effects in the ~8 wt.% Al variant are attributed to the formation of nm-sized κ-carbides during aging (b0025).
κ-carbides are thermally very stable at 600 °C and even prevail after 100 h heat treatment with only modest coarsening (b0025).

The 8Al (purple) series in Fig. 4 reaches the highest tensile strength (~800–950 MPa) among the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl alloys, with higher Al content and aging shifting the alloy toward higher strength at reduced elongation (figure_004).
After aging at 500–600 °C, twinning is reduced and strain hardening is essentially associated with κ-carbide and solid-solution strengthening (b0031).

Proposed deformation mechanism for steels strengthened by regularly arranged nanosized κ-carbides: Orowan bypassing of longitudinal κ-carbide rods, subsequent expansion of dislocation loops assisted by cross-slip, and to a minor extent shearing of κ-carbides (b0032).
